disadvantages: The module is large and mixes field declarations with resolution helpers, so it is slow to read and easy to over-extend.

name: Strict TOML file loader
description: Parses the TOML file into the configuration, using the field set passed in by the dataclass, and raises a configuration-file error on anything a file cannot express: unknown keys, adapter-only objects and malformed values. The personas table is read here as a structured section.
advantages: Fails loudly and early with the offending key named, which removes silent typos.
disadvantages: Strictness means any new field must be registered as file-expressible before it can be used, and it cannot express live objects such as adapters.

name: Environment and env-file layering
description: Applies environment files and the file's own environment tables to the process with defined precedence: a process variable beats env files, which beat the file's environment table, and an earlier env file wins over a later one. It also treats blank placeholder values as unset so defaults still apply.
advantages: Lets one file serve as a baseline while an operator overrides a single value without editing it; precedence is deterministic.
disadvantages: Mutating the process environment is a global side effect, so ordering bugs show up as action at a distance and tests must scrub the environment.

name: Environment-backed tuning settings
description: Parses the tunables the core package needs (timeouts, caps, floors, review interval) from the environment into one typed settings value, falling back to the shipped default on a bad value and allowing zero to switch a feature off. The provider re-reads the environment on each call unless a fixed value is pinned.
advantages: A malformed value can never stop a lane, and a running process can be retuned without a restart.
disadvantages: Silent fallback hides a typo in a tuning value, unlike the loud rejection used for file keys; re-reading on every call costs a little work per use.

name: Injected core settings holder
description: Defines the typed settings value and the install and read functions, so the core package asks for its tunables at the point of use instead of touching the process environment. A consumer can pin a fixed value or supply a provider.
advantages: Keeps the core package free of environment reads and makes it testable with fixed settings.
disadvantages: Core code relies on a globally installed provider, so a missing install gives surprising defaults.

name: Layered configuration evaluation arm
description: Drives the live loaders offline: the file alone through the from-file constructor, the layered startup path through the same function the command line uses, and the tuning settings, scrubbing the process environment and faking nothing else. It is the measured arm for the real configuration path, scored on rule-by-rule cases.
advantages: Exercises the real code, so a precedence regression fails a case directly, with zero model calls. Selected because: cli_config._config_from_env (QAR_CONFIG_FILE or --config)
disadvantages: Covers the commonly set scalar fields, not every field, so a rarely used field can regress unnoticed.

name: Command dispatcher
description: The entry point builds the parser, routes each subcommand to its handler and converts outcomes into exit codes. Store commands and Quest commands are delegated to their own modules so the dispatcher stays a thin router.
advantages: One entry point gives a consistent exit-code contract across all subcommands.
disadvantages: It also hosts interactive surfaces that are not scored, so a regression there is not caught by the offline cases.

name: Declarative argument tree
description: Defines the whole argparse tree for every subcommand in one place, with help text and flag definitions, so parsing and usage errors come from the parser itself.
advantages: Help and refusal behaviour for unknown commands and flags is uniform and cheap to test.
disadvantages: Behaviour that depends on cross-flag rules lives in handlers, not here, so the parser alone does not guarantee valid combinations.

name: Quest API subcommands
description: Implements the generic quest command, send, reconcile-plan, create-goal and folder sync by introspecting the Quest client's methods, refusing write methods unless a write flag is given, and parsing keyword pairs as JSON when possible.
advantages: A new client method becomes callable from the shell without new CLI code, with a safe read-only default.
disadvantages: Introspection means the help text is only as good as the client docstrings, and a pair value that happens to parse as JSON is not passed as a string.

name: Card-store maintenance commands
description: Provides the context subcommands for moving a store root, migrating imports, merging stores, showing info and uploading a local store, all as a dry run unless an apply flag is given, and none of them embeds anything.
advantages: Dry-run by default protects stores from accidental change and shows what would happen.
disadvantages: Operations on real stores and vector points are hard to simulate fully, so most of the risk is covered only on a scratch folder.

name: Tool catalog shell entry
description: Lets a deep run's shell list, show and call the same tools the brain uses in process, rebuilding the catalog from the lane's environment and accepting arguments as keyword pairs or one JSON object, with keyword pairs winning.
advantages: A shell can use the same tools as the brain with no second implementation, and custom tools appear automatically.
disadvantages: Argument typing by JSON guessing can surprise a caller, and a call acts for real when the tool does.

name: Real-entry-point evaluation arm
description: Calls the live main functions in process with a scrubbed environment and a scratch folder, capturing output and exit code, and fakes nothing. It is the measured arm for the command-line surface.
advantages: Tests the actual entry points end to end without a subprocess, so it is fast and offline. Selected because: pyproject console script quest-ai-runner and python -m quest_ai_runner.tools
disadvantages: In-process calls do not cover the console-script wrapper or terminal behaviour, and interactive modes are out of reach.

name: Difficulty-to-rung starter
description: Turns the planner's difficulty rating into a starting rung on the deep-worker ladder, normalising synonyms and unknown ratings and respecting an operator mapping, with no additional model call.
advantages: Free at runtime because it reuses a rating the planner already produced.
disadvantages: Quality depends entirely on the planner's rating, and hard work is not started on a stronger rung by default.

name: Live tier registry
description: Maps a tier name to the newest live model id by bucketing a provider's latest-first list by family, caching the result, using a last-known fallback only when the live list is empty, and exposing the next lower tier and vision capability.
advantages: Tracks new releases automatically and never fails resolution when the provider is unreachable.
disadvantages: The fallback map can go stale, and bucketing by family substring depends on provider naming conventions.

name: Family-name resolver
description: Resolves a bare family name to the newest live release of that family for any vendor, passing anything that names a pinned release through untouched.
advantages: Configuration that names only a family never needs editing when a release ships.
disadvantages: Version ordering is parsed from the id text, so an unusual naming scheme can pick the wrong release.

name: Provider outage recognition and wait
description: Classifies an exception as a provider overload or outage, remembers the latest one, and supplies a resume time a few minutes ahead so the executor can requeue the task with a hold reason instead of failing it.
advantages: Turns a transient environment failure into a visible, automatic retry with nothing lost.
disadvantages: Classification is by exception shape and wording, so a new provider error form is missed until added.

name: Subscription allowance limit detector
description: Detects a subscription usage-limit message in a run's result, parses its reset time and zone, computes a resume time, and records the limit lane-wide with optional persistence so other work waits.
advantages: Resumes after the real reset instead of retrying uselessly, and survives a restart when persistence is configured.
disadvantages: Depends on parsing human-readable wording and time zones, which can change without notice.

name: Live selection evaluation arm
description: Calls the live selection, family, registry, fallback, outage and limit functions with a provider fake that only lists models. It is the measured arm for the rules above.
advantages: Checks every rule against real code offline, with zero model calls. Selected because: core/selection_table.py via ModelRegistry and orchestrator_deep_models
disadvantages: Proves the chosen model follows the rules, not that it was the cheapest that still succeeded.

name: Static price table lookup
description: Holds a snapshot of list prices per million input tokens by provider and model, detects the provider from the environment, falls back to a stated default for unknown models, and estimates bootstrap cost from a token count.
advantages: Simple, offline and instant, and gives a cost estimate before any spend.
disadvantages: Hand-maintained, input tokens only, and stale until someone edits it.

name: Persisted daily token tracker
description: Counts input and output tokens within a UTC day, persists the tally to a JSON file so a restart reloads it, resets at the day boundary, and reports over-limit and a status line. A limit of zero or off disables it.
advantages: Survives restarts and cleanly separates days; opt-in so it never surprises a lane.
disadvantages: Counts tokens, not money, and a deep runner on a subscription is outside the count; a lost usage file resets the day.

name: Hysteresis resource guard
description: Samples memory use, free memory and load, pauses new work when a limit is exceeded and resumes only after readings clear, and can wait until the host is fine. Sampling uses the process file system or a library, with limits from code or the environment.
advantages: Hysteresis prevents flapping, and pausing is lossless because unclaimed work stays queued.
disadvantages: Thresholds are manual and host-specific, and the sampler depends on platform facilities that may be absent.

name: Live usage evaluation arm
description: Drives the live price, estimate, tracker and guard code, with a real usage file in a scratch folder and scripted host samples as the only fake.
advantages: Verifies arithmetic and persistence against real code with no model calls. Selected because: runner/poller.py (ResourceGuard, DailyUsageTracker) and cli_context bootstrap estimate
disadvantages: Cannot notice that real prices have changed, only that the table is internally right.

advantages: Selected because: CLAUDE.md pre-commit rule: run only the tests your change touches; this collection check is the cheap whole-suite gate

name: Planted-secret evaluation arm
description: Runs the live scanner on text assembled from fragments (so the test file itself is clean), on groups of real repository files, and as a command in a throwaway git repository.
advantages: Proves both detection and silence on placeholders against the real scanner, without keeping real secrets anywhere. Selected because: `esoi hygiene` (CLAUDE.md pre-commit step 2, docs/public-hygiene.md)
disadvantages: Planted cases only cover the shapes someone thought to add.

advantages: Selected because: core/resolve.py resolve() over the declarations beside each implementation and the records (S30)

name: Documentation index
description: The index document that groups tutorials, guides and references and links every other document, so a reader or an AI starts in one place and every document is reachable.
advantages: A single entry point makes orphan detection simple and onboarding quick.
disadvantages: Needs manual upkeep, and a linked document may still be unclear or outdated.

name: Shipped-documents evaluation arm
description: Resolves relative links on disk, counts em dashes, reads the index and the generated configuration reference, and consults the live package for its public names and real subcommands to confirm each is documented.
advantages: Checks the docs as shipped against the live code, with zero model calls. Selected because: docs/README.md (the index), docs/configuration.md (generated), README.md
disadvantages: Checks presence and form, not whether a description is accurate or helpful.

name: Atomic file prediction store
description: Keeps one JSON file per scope, written atomically, plus an append-only outcome log, drops expired predictions on load and swallows storage errors so a failure never reaches a turn.
advantages: Durable across restarts and isolated per scope, with no external service. Selected because: fixed in code
disadvantages: Single-host files do not share across machines and need cleanup of old scope files; best-effort swallowing can hide a failing disk.

name: In-memory reference store
description: Satisfies the same port with plain dictionaries, giving a reference a consumer with its own database can match.
advantages: Trivial and fast, useful as a contract reference and in tests.
disadvantages: Keeps nothing across store objects, so it fails the restart scenario by design and is not suitable for production. The in-memory reference fails the restart scenario by design.

name: Eligibility gate mixin
description: Methods on the autopilot pass that test, in order, daily budget, cadence in the quest's zone, Run now, reactive trigger, roster day and backpressure, and read open asks, so a quest is skipped with a reason before any goal is read.
advantages: Cheap, ordered and explainable gates that follow the person's settings exactly.
disadvantages: The ordering and interplay of many rules is intricate, and a new setting needs a matching case.

name: Scripted-client gate evaluation arm
description: Runs the production autopilot pass for one quest against a client that answers only what a gate reads and a pinned clock, recording anything reached past the gates, so the outcome is exactly a skip reason or passage.
advantages: Tests the real gates deterministically with no model calls. Selected because: runner/autopilot_gates.py GatesMixin._gate_quest, the budget check in AutopilotPass.run and the pure predicates in runner/autopilot_periods.py
disadvantages: Measures only the decision to run, not the work after it.

name: Apply the evolvable-structure library
description: QAR keeps its specifications as records under esoi and builds on the library's solutions to apply a project's structure: the application procedure, the structure check, the measurement harness and the implementation selector.
advantages: No checker of QAR's own to maintain; every part is compared on the same cases and selected by its metric. Selected because: the evolvable-structure library already carries the machinery; QAR keeps only its records and configuration
disadvantages: A dependency pinned by commit

name: Prompts without the intent frame
description: Quest-scoped prompts carry the quest alone: its outcome, current state and preferences, with no mention of the intent it serves.
advantages: Zero added tokens and nothing to go wrong. Selected because: Nothing is measured yet: the frame ships behind no switch because it costs nothing for people without intents, and the no-frame arm stays selected until the metric decides
disadvantages: Choices and judgments ignore the person's top intents, and gaps under an intent go unnoticed.

name: Computed frame in the prompt
description: The server computes a short frame from stored ids and the autopilot brief, the chat quest facts and the quest card carry it; no model call.
advantages: Cheap, deterministic, and empty for people without intents.
disadvantages: Gives the model only names and links; it cannot answer detailed questions about the specification without a drill-down.

name: Frame plus intent card and record drill-down
description: The frame, one context card per top intent chosen by relevance, and a get_spec read that returns the best-matching records for a question.
advantages: Answers questions about the specification by meaning and pays tokens only for what a turn uses.
disadvantages: More moving parts; the card must be kept in step with the intent and the drill-down must rank records well.

name: Frame plus a lazily generated quest specification
description: The frame plus one model-written specification of a ready quest, generated the first time an AI consumer needs it, reachable through the drill-down.
advantages: Adds what the quest's own fields cannot say: dimension ideals, links and sufficiency gaps.
disadvantages: One model call per used quest and a risk of restating fields the quest already holds.

name: Generic method in the standing instructions
description: Every deep run carries the same principles as required standing instructions, whatever the task serves.
advantages: Carries the author's principles into every run with nothing to build.
disadvantages: Large, and says nothing about the problem, ideal or metric the task serves.

name: Slice of the specification before the task
description: The brief gets the slice for the quest or solution the task serves, with the standing instructions kept short.
advantages: Specific to the task and small.
disadvantages: Needs a source for the slice for each kind of specification; built for a repository's ESOI records only.

name: Slice before and write-back after
description: The slice before the task, and the runner reads the metric before and after the work and writes the readings to the run's metric ledger, beside any result the worker records. The readings go to a per-run file of readings in a temporary folder (the metric ledger of docs/metric-results.md, core/metric_results.py) and onto the task report; a card's usage_count and last_outcome are set by FileContextStore.record from the kind of turn.
advantages: Closes the loop so the next task starts from what this one learned. Selected because: Joshua directed on 2026-10-21 that every run's metric result before and after is recorded by code; the replay metric (task_replay) is not built, so this is a direction, not a measured win.
disadvantages: Needs the measured replay to confirm it helps. Readings expire with the temporary folder and never reach the record; nothing says what moved; nothing makes a run fix a record it found wrong; a card's outcome is not tied to any metric.

name: Slice before and write-back onto each record (planned)
description: Planned. The slice before the task as in slice-and-writeback; after it, the run's readings are appended to the results log with the run and the solution. A record the run found wrong or missing is edited directly in the same commit as the work, with the reason in the commit message, and the record's row in esoi/tracker/ (the review files esoi tracker build writes, one row per record) gets its tracking columns updated: last run in tracking_updated, outcome in tracking_status, movement, what moved and the reason for any change in tracking_notes. A card gets the same in usage_count, last_outcome and provenance. Only a change to the owner's own words (an intent's vision statement, the ideals the owner wrote) is raised as a proposal, and only the escalation triggers raise a decision request.
advantages: One source of truth per kind, no new file per run, specifications kept current by the runs that use them, and people asked only when a change needs them.
disadvantages: The tracking columns are filled by hand today, so a machine writer needs a lock for concurrent runs; a wrong edit is caught only by review of the history or by the metric; a run with no offline arm still has only a recorded reading.

name: Classify through the message router alternatives
description: Quest classification of a request (answer, tool, deep, confirm, clarify, and the tool and arguments) is done by the four recorded alternatives of route-a-message (full planner, cheap pre-route then planner, single prompt, keyword rules), scored on the classification cases.
advantages: Four real alternatives already exist and are compared on the labelled classification cases by one scorer; no new code.
disadvantages: Covers classifying a message, not choosing which quest an ask belongs to or recommending the next goal, step or quest; those two tasks still lack labelled cases and an alternative.

name: Route with the registry of examples, by model tier
description: The backend's intent routing conditioned on a registry of labelled examples, run on the cheapest tier or a stronger one, with or without the registry (quest-backend qar_eval/intent_routing.py; arms registry_haiku and registry_sonnet).
advantages: Recorded in quest-backend esoi/quest-ai/results.csv on its held-out and registry cases: haiku scores the same as sonnet at about a third of the cost.
disadvantages: Backend-side and a small case set in the recorded run; not yet run on which-quest or recommendation cases.

name: Pick the quest with the shared ranker (embeddings lead, the model picks by number)
description: Which quest a piece of text belongs to, for every surface that picks one: daily plan goals, reflection notes, insights' quests field, the AI task form, chat task pickup and task delegation. The quests' own embeddings lead the candidates, the model only picks which numbered quests a text is about (or none), and the user's priority orders them. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_selection.py (rank_quest_batch, select_and_rank_quests_for_text).
advantages: One shared path, so a better pick improves every surface at once; a wrong quest is answered with none, not a guess; a few output tokens per text.
disadvantages: No labelled case set or recorded accuracy yet, only unit tests (tests/api/endpoints/daily_plan/test_rank_goal_quests.py, tests/test_reflection_notes_ranker_failure.py). Its past alternatives were replaced without a measured comparison: the model ordering the quests (before e1736906), each surface prompting its own pick such as the daily plan prompt (before 9b1c791b), and the first-priority quest as the fallback (before 7fb9cfec).

name: Rank quests by words and meaning, with evidence
description: Ranks a person's own quests for a chat message by IDF-weighted word overlap plus embedding similarity, with the model judging which terms actually identify a quest, and returns evidence snippets saying where each match came from. Used by Quest AI chat to resolve which quest a message names. quest-backend app/business/quests/quest_candidates.py (rank_quests_for_message, lexical_rank, semantic_quest_candidates).
advantages: Shows its evidence, so the caller can show its work instead of asserting a match; the lexical signal catches named quests that embeddings blur.
disadvantages: A second classifier doing much of the same job as shared-quest-ranker, on a different code path; never compared with it on the same cases (tests/test_quest_candidates.py are unit tests).

name: Match a goal to an area of life by vector similarity
description: Classifies a new quest's goal text into a planet (area of life) and town (subcategory) by Qdrant vector similarity; in top-level mode a planet scores the best similarity of itself or any of its towns. Used in quest creation and the dashboard category edit. quest-backend app/api/endpoints/categories/search.py (suggest_category_from_goal). Older alternatives still in the code: planets_service.suggest_planet_for_quest and suggest_towns_for_quest (vector search with 0.7 and 0.6 thresholds; their endpoints are marked deprecated in quest-frontend api.config.ts) and the CategoryCache prefix search.
advantages: No model call, so it is fast and nearly free; the max over towns lifts the right planet when a goal names something specific.
disadvantages: Accuracy is unmeasured beyond tests/api/endpoints/categories/test_suggest_from_goal_top_level.py; the max-over-towns rule and the older thresholded alternatives were never scored against each other.

name: Place quests under top intents with the model
description: Proposes which of a person's top intents each existing quest belongs under, with a reason and a confidence, in batches of ten on the balanced tier. Used in onboarding's last step. quest-backend app/business/intents/suggest.py (suggest_placements).
advantages: Reads each quest as a whole and explains its choice; nothing is applied until the person accepts, so every accept or change is a free label.
disadvantages: Balanced tier on every batch, never tried on the cheapest tier or against the embedding rankers above; accepted and changed placements are not yet collected as cases.

name: Recommend top intents with the model
description: Recommends three to five top intents from what a person wrote in onboarding, saying which of their items each one covers. quest-backend app/business/intents/suggest.py (suggest_intents).
advantages: Covers every item the person listed and reports the ones left uncovered.
disadvantages: One implementation, no alternative and no recorded acceptance rate.

name: Recommend where backlog goals go in the next period
description: Recommends which backlog goals to place in which slot of the next week, month or quarter, seeing slip counts, the quest's state, saved period notes and the goals already placed there. Used by period review planning. quest-backend app/services/ai/period_review_ai.py (suggest_placements).
advantages: Uses the person's own history (slips, peers in the same slot) rather than a generic schedule.
disadvantages: One implementation; how many of its placements people keep is not recorded.

name: Lexical TF-IDF, optional vector search, parallel batched model judging
description: Field-weighted TF-IDF over the index's own terms proposes candidates; an injected vector search proposes more, fused by reciprocal rank; the candidates' one-line descriptions are cut into batches and a cheap model judges all batches in parallel; ids not offered are dropped, a failed batch keeps its candidates, and each selected record brings its links.
advantages: Words, meaning and judgement each do what they are good at; latency is one call; degrades to the lexical candidates when a model or vector call fails.
disadvantages: Costs one cheap model call per batch of candidates; the vector search is the consumer's to supply.

name: Lexical top few only
description: The best few lexical matches and their links, with no vector search and no model.
advantages: Free and instant; the baseline for what the rest adds.
disadvantages: Misses a record that shares no word with the request, and cannot tell a keyword match that does not apply.

name: Lexical vector gated
description: Lexical plus vector candidates, then a confidence gate: a clear case is answered from the two searches' agreement and an empty case returns nothing, both with no model call; every other request costs one call that judges the best ``GATE_POOL`` candidates together. Cheaper and faster than judging every request in batches, with the model kept for the requests that need it. With no provider the ambiguous requests return the best fused candidates.
advantages: One model call (or none) per request instead of one per batch: a clear case and an empty case are answered from the two searches alone, so it is cheaper and faster than judging every request. Selected because: the 2026-10-20 run of metric-spec-selection on the labelled requests (the results log has the commit and the cases) ranked lexical-vector-gated first on the balanced score, above lexical-vector-llm (which returned a crowd), lexical-vector and lexical-only
disadvantages: The gate thresholds are tuned on this dataset and can answer a clear-looking wrong case without a model's check; needs a vector search that returns scores.

name: Card quarantine tool
description: scripts/quarantine_cards.py reads a store and moves cards out of its index into the quarantine folder by reason: compounded copies (two or more import namespaces in the id) when a surviving card with the same files stays, cards mostly under folders the folder review excludes, surplus cards pinning the same files as a kept card, and thin cards over one generated data file. The arm runs the script with --apply over each fixture store; tests/test_quarantine_cards.py pins what it must not do.
advantages: Repairs a store that already inflated with no lane restart and no re-embedding; reversible; keeps taught and managed cards; a dry run and a manifest show every move first.
disadvantages: Runs after the fact and by an operator; does not stop the next pass from re-importing; reads a local folder store only, not the Quest backend.

name: Store as copy mode leaves it
description: Nothing is run over the store, so every namespaced copy a pass added stays in the index.
advantages: Costs nothing and touches nothing: the floor a growth control must beat.
disadvantages: Grows with every re-import pass; duplicates crowd the view, and every copy is fingerprinted and embedded again.

name: Bootstrap guards against re-import
description: Committed on 2026-10-22 in the library itself (commit 3a59e57, with the review fixes of commits a1fff6f, 2b8e379 and ac61f64): a copy's id is made of its origin, so it cannot grow by hop and a store never imports its own cards; a store is never its own import source; every repository write refuses an id that repeats a namespace segment or is a vector point id; indexing under a root other than the store's recorded one is refused; a copy pinning the same files as a card the store holds is not kept; and the card limit (adapters/card_limit.py, QAR_MAX_CARDS, 1000 by default, 0 removes it) refuses new derived cards at the limit and announces it. The tidy at open (self_heal, adapters/context_store_heal.py) is part of the change, but the runner's builders pass self_heal off since commit 6980d7c, so the arms run the store with the setting the runner ships, read from config_assembler.py: the card_growth arm opens an inflated store as the runner opens it, and card_store_growth builds stores through repeated passes.
advantages: Stops compounding at its cause, on every backend, with no operator step; a refused write is logged as an error naming the id; the limit never deletes and always says what fills the store and how to change it.
disadvantages: As shipped it does not repair a store that already inflated: with the tidy off, copies an older version left behind stay until the cleanup tool is run. Growth paths found by two reviews on 2026-10-22 and still open in committed code: copy mode is still the default (QAR_CARD_MOUNT, card_store_mounts.mount_mode_from_env); two stores keep their own folder reviews, which can disagree on the same folder with nothing reconciling them; quarantining or evicting a card leaves its vector point behind, and only context migrate-imports --prune-points removes points; and a lone backup snapshot under the corpus (one store, no dated series beside it) carries its own .quest-context and is still imported when the folder review cannot run, because a folder with no risk signal fails open. Closed since the reviews: what may never be moved is one definition (card_origin.protection, commit a1fff6f) that protects a card with no provenance, notes a run added, quest tags or conventions; a copy someone added to joins its replacement before it is retired (commit 2b8e379); and one risk gate (context_risk_gate.folder_gate, commit ac61f64) is asked by the walk, nested and ancestor imports and mounts, so ancestor imports now follow the folder review and a folder holding many stores or a series of dated copies is not read when the review cannot run.

name: Two pipelines side by side (today)
description: select-context assembles cards into every run's context, and spec-selection answers the find_specs family of tools and the deep-goal slice, each with its own index, stages, budget and output.
advantages: Both are built and measured; each is tuned to its own kind of item.
disadvantages: Duplicated stages and model calls; records are not in a run's context unless it calls a tool; no shared budget; card results carry no kind.

name: Every record kind ranked beside cards (planned)
description: Planned. Each ESOI record (intent, problem, ideal, solution, metric) is a read-only view keyed by source and record id, read from esoi/*.csv at query time and ranked with the cards in one lexical stage, one vector stage, one fusion and one gated model choice.
advantages: Simplest merge: one candidate pool, nothing about records left out of ranking.
disadvantages: Intents, ideals and metrics compete for the budget with the items a run acts on; a run may get the why without the solution it serves; more candidates for the model to judge. It does reach a request that matches only an ideal or a metric.

name: Cards, solutions and problems ranked; intents, ideals and metrics reached through links
description: Cards, solution records and problem records are ranked together. A solution brings its ideals, its metrics and its intent's frame; a problem brings its ideals and its intent. When the best match is a problem or an intent with no solution, the result says "no solution yet" and the run defines one. A quest, being an intent, is reached through the ground-in-intent frame. Built in quest_ai_runner/core/unified_search.py (cards from a store through adapters/card_views.py) and reached through the read-only tool search_cards_and_specs beside find_specs; tags filter or boost, off by default.
advantages: Ranks what a run acts on (cards, solutions) and where new work starts (problems); the why arrives with what it explains; a missing solution becomes a visible cue instead of an empty result.
disadvantages: A request that matches only an ideal or a metric, with no matching problem or solution, finds nothing; an intent with no problem or solution is not reachable; depends on links being complete. An implementation named in a request is reached only after a solution's ideal, metric and intent links, so the default link budget leaves it out.

name: Problem-linked tag list with a check rule and a lookup
description: esoi/tags.csv holds each tag with a one-sentence meaning and the problems it mitigates (problem_ids); solutions carry tags in their tags column; the QAR rule Q1 in scripts/esoi_tags.py (registered by the plugin scripts/esoi_rules.py) fails a tag outside the list, a listed tag with no meaning, with no linked problem or with a linked id that is not a problem record, and a tag used by no solution or by every solution, and prints a note for a tag on one solution. tags_of and solutions_sharing (and the script run as a command) read a solution's tags as its column plus its problem_ids.
advantages: One list as the source of truth; every tag's risk is a problem record that can be read, linked and solved; the lookup uses the links that already exist, so problem ids are never copied.
disadvantages: The rule cannot judge whether a tag mitigates its risk or whether a link already identifies the same solutions; that rests on the back-fill procedure and, later, on the metric. R1 to R4 are recorded in this project, not yet in the library that owns them.

name: Risk-gated folder review
description: Committed in the library (adapters/context_risk_gate.py, commit ac61f64; the arm calls folder_gate unchanged). One cheap walk gathers structural signals with no model: three or more card stores under one folder, a series of three or more sibling folders named like dates, timestamps or versions that share one child structure, and a very large folder. A folder with a signal is always put to the folder review, below the file-count floor too, with the signal in the prompt; the verdict is cached in folder_review.json with source risk_signal and stays human-editable. When the review cannot run, a folder with a stores or series signal is not indexed, not entered, and no store beneath it is imported or mounted, with one warning naming the override. Ancestor stores in a series of copies are ignored the same way. Every card source asks this one function, and everything without a signal keeps the review as it was.
advantages: Keeps a snapshot series out whether or not a model is available, at the cost of one batched review call for the flagged folders; one answer for every card source; the legitimate nested store and ordinary folders are untouched; a person overrides it in the same file as every other verdict.
disadvantages: Open weaknesses: two stores keep their own folder_review.json, which can disagree on the same folder with nothing reconciling them; the large-folder signal never blocks by itself, so a huge folder with no copies is read in full when the review cannot run; a lone backup snapshot (one store, no series beside it) is still imported when the review cannot run, and below the file-count floor a correct skip verdict is never asked for it; a reviewer or person answering index is obeyed, so a wrong model verdict lets the series in; and it has not been run over a real backups folder of 155 stores, only over the fixture.

name: Model-judged folder review before the gate
description: The folder review as it was before the risk gate (review_corpus with no risk signals, still reachable as _folder_review): below a floor of 2,000 indexable files nothing is judged; above it the nested-repository and duplicate-tree safeguards run without a model, then batched model calls judge folders shallow first and open up only large kept or mixed ones, with verdicts cached in folder_review.json. If the review is off, has no provider or fails, nothing is excluded.
advantages: Cheap: a few batched calls per corpus, per folder not per file; keeps an unreviewable ordinary corpus fully indexed; a correct model above the floor keeps the snapshots out.
disadvantages: Fails open exactly where the risk is: with no model, the review switched off or a failed call, every snapshot store is imported or mounted and every snapshot is walked; below the floor the snapshots are never even asked about; and it decides only for the file walk's ordinary folders, so nothing names a series of copies as the reason.

name: Index everything (broken baseline)
description: No folder decision: extension filtering and the skip list only, so every folder is walked and every card store found is imported or mounted.
advantages: No model call and no rule to get wrong; nothing real is ever left out.
disadvantages: Every snapshot of a backups folder becomes cards, imports or mounts, which is the incident itself; kept only as the floor the cases must fail.
